title: The Emerging U.S.-China Détente
gist: A senior Tsinghua strategist argues that the Xi-Trump meeting in Beijing in May 2026 produced the first mutually recognized definition of the U.S.-China relationship in over a decade — 'strategic stability' meaning a new equilibrium rather than nuclear détente — and that Washington's reflex to dismiss it as empty words is a misreading.

insights.claim: At their May 2026 Beijing meeting, Xi Jinping and Donald Trump agreed their countries should build a constructive relationship of strategic stability, the first time in more than a decade that Beijing and Washington have shared a definition of the relationship that leaders on both sides broadly recognize.
insights.speaker: Da Wei
insights.so_what: A shared bilateral framing is the precondition for tariff and export-control de-escalation; watch for follow-through in trade and tech restrictions rather than in the communiqué language.
insights.quote: it marks the first time in more than a decade that China and the United States established a consensus about how to define the relationship that leaders on both sides broadly recognize
insights.locator: When Chinese leader Xi Jinping and U.S. President

insights.claim: 'Strategic stability' in this context does not mean nuclear détente but a new equilibrium in which both sides can avoid further escalation.
insights.speaker: Da Wei
insights.so_what: Prevents mis-pricing the deal as an arms-control breakthrough; the tradable content is economic and escalation management, not warheads.
insights.quote: Strategic stability does not refer to nuclear détente; rather, it suggests a new equilibrium
insights.locator: Strategic stability does not refer to nuclear détente

insights.claim: Many observers in Washington dismissed the new strategic-stability framework as empty words, a skepticism that a leading Chinese security scholar treats as the main obstacle to the détente holding.
insights.speaker: Da Wei
insights.so_what: Consensus positioning still assumes structural U.S.-China deterioration; if the détente is real, China-exposed equities and trade-sensitive supply chains are mispriced to the downside.
insights.quote: Although many observers in Washington responded skeptically to this new framework, dismissing it as empty words
insights.locator: Although many observers in Washington responded skeptically

insights.claim: The stable configuration being proposed pairs a confident Beijing with a pragmatic Washington, implying China is negotiating from perceived strength rather than from a need for relief.
insights.speaker: Da Wei
insights.so_what: If Beijing believes it holds the stronger hand, expect it to concede less in trade talks than U.S. negotiators assume — a risk to deal-driven rallies.
insights.quote: A Confident Beijing and a Pragmatic Washington Can Get Along
insights.locator: A Confident Beijing and a Pragmatic Washington Can Get Along
